title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Myanmar: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Myanmar: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Myanmar: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: Planning medical, legal, and financial administration ahead of time for a person living with serious or terminal illness in Myanmar requires careful local verification because ongoing armed conflict and restricted or unreliable domestic ministry web infrastructure mean many Myanmar government portals (including Ministry of Health and Social Security Board sites) are offline, incomplete, or geo-restricted from abroad [1][2]. To offer reliable statutory context despite restricted online government portals, core rules on civil registration, succession, Powers of Attorney, disability rights, and the Social Security Law 2012 are cited here from ILO NATLEX, Online Burma/Myanmar Library, Myanmar Law Library, and UN ESCAP alongside official foreign reciprocity documentation (travel.state.gov and GOV.UK), with a practical warning to verify current procedures directly at local Township Administration and Township Health offices [1][2][5][6][8][10].

steps.title: Palliative care documentation, consent, and identity records
steps.html:
• Medical records and hospital consent practice: Public and private hospitals in Myanmar do not operate a statutory advance-directive registry; recording treatment preferences in writing with the treating medical team and designating one primary family spokesperson streamlines inpatient care and billing [2][3].
  • Disability assessment and support documentation: Under the Law on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (Pyidaungsu Hluttaw Law No. 30/2015), patients experiencing chronic severe functional impairment can apply for formal disability registration and medical-board documentation to support rehabilitation and assistive-care access, although conflict sharply limits local funding [11].
  • Securing Household Registration and Citizenship cards: Ensuring the patient's National Registration Card (Naing-Ngan-Tha-Si-Sit-Yay-Kat) and Household Registration List (Ein Daung Su Sayin) match family names at the Township Public Health Office and Township General Administration Department avoids future hospital or court rejections [1][5].

steps.title: Powers of attorney and registration rules before incapacity
steps.html:
• Statutory basis under the Powers of Attorney Act: Granting a representative legal authority to manage bank accounts, pension filings, or property matters is governed by the Powers of Attorney Act (India Act VII of 1882) together with instrument authentication rules under the Registration Act (1909) [8][9].
  • Executing and registering a Power of Attorney: Inside Myanmar, Powers of Attorney affecting immovable property or major financial mandates must be notarized or registered through the Office of the Registration of Deeds and Township Notaries (Powers of Attorney Act) while the principal retains sound mental capacity [8][9].
  • Consular execution from abroad: Principals residing overseas who need an agent inside Myanmar normally execute a Power of Attorney before a Myanmar embassy (or locally notarized and consularly legalized) and have the agent register it locally, though international diplomatic and banking channels face heightened practical scrutiny [1][9].

steps.title: Wills, plural succession rules, and estate preparation
steps.html:
• Personal religious law under Burma Laws Act 1898: Under Section 13 of the Burma Laws Act (1898), inheritance depends on the person's religious community: Myanmar Customary Law applies to Buddhists (under which testamentary wills generally do not override statutory family inheritance rights for spouse and children), Islamic law applies to Muslims (ordinarily capping wills at one-third of the net estate), and Hindu law applies to Hindus [6].
  • Succession Act 1925 for Christians and civil wills: Christians, Parsis, and civil estates governed by the Succession Act (India Act XXXIX of 1925) may execute formal attested wills nominating an executor, which later require probate from District and Township Civil Courts (Succession Act and Personal Law) [7].
  • Gathering deeds, land grants, and bank records: Organizing property leases (Gayan), tax receipts, and bank account statements early spares relatives complex court reconstruction if local land offices face conflict disruptions [6][7][9].

steps.title: Social Security Law 2012 disability benefits and employment leave
steps.html:
• Social Security Board (SSB) invalidity and medical care: Insured private-sector and state-enterprise employees should confirm active contribution records with local Social Security Board (SSB) Township Offices (Social Security Law 2012) covering sickness cash benefits, medical care, permanent invalidity pensions, and future survivor coverage under Pyidaungsu Hluttaw Law No. 15/2012 [10].
  • Statutory medical leave: Formal-sector employees undergoing extended treatment retain earned, casual, and medical leave protections under the Leave and Holidays Act (as amended by SPDC Law No. 6/2006), provided stamped medical certificates are submitted promptly to employers [4].
  • Operational caveat in conflict zones: Because administrative closures and banking restrictions interrupt benefit payouts outside major urban townships, families should keep certified physical copies of SSB registration cards and contribution books [1][10].

steps.title: Civil-registry alignment and consular legalization (non-Apostille)
steps.html:
• Vital records readiness: Keeping original household lists, birth records, and notarized Burmese-to-English translations synchronized with Township Public Health Office and Township General Administration Department files prevents bottlenecks under Myanmar's civil registration system [1][3][5].
  • Non-Apostille treaty status: According to the Hague Conference on Private International Law (HCCH) status table, Myanmar is not a Contracting Party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention; an Apostille stamp has no legal effect in Myanmar [12].
  • Consular legalization workflow: Any Power of Attorney, medical certificate, or civil record transmitted between Myanmar and another country requires sequential consular legalization involving local notarial certification, the Myanmar Ministry of Foreign Affairs Consular Department in Naypyidaw or Yangon, and the relevant foreign embassy or consulate [1][2][3][12].

prefillQuestion: A family member is facing a serious or terminal illness in Myanmar. We need an overview of the main official steps and contacts in Myanmar for palliative care, powers of attorney, advance directives, and caregiver support.

contacts.name: Township Public Health Office and Township General Administration Department
contacts.note: Local township administration and public health offices maintaining vital records and Ward or Village Tract confirmations.

contacts.name: Office of the Registration of Deeds and Township Notaries (Powers of Attorney Act)
contacts.note: Deed registries and public notaries authenticating and registering Powers of Attorney and property instruments under the 1882 and 1909 Acts.

contacts.name: Social Security Board (SSB) Township Offices (Social Security Law 2012)
contacts.note: Local offices managing insured workers' sickness cash benefits, medical coverage, invalidity pensions, and survivor coverage.

contacts.name: District and Township Civil Courts (Succession Act and Personal Law)
contacts.note: Civil courts exercising jurisdiction over personal-law inheritance under Section 13 of the Burma Laws Act 1898 and wills under the Succession Act 1925.
